transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-23
Start time (UTC): 15:30
Duration: 1h15m (scheduled)
Attendees: Maya Brooks (PM), Jordan Lee (Infra Eng), Claire Nguyen (SRE), Ethan Zhao (Runtime Eng), Luis Ortega (QA)

Summary:
Quick sprint sync to finalize shipday safety-net (staged eviction + graceful degrade), telemetry gaps, and runbook items before the July 30 internal launch. Focus on three risk areas: kernel fallback behavior under quantized models, surge queue bypasses, and alert noise.

Topics:
- Runbook scope & ownership
- Telemetry gaps / dashboarding needs
- Kernel fallback tests and known model regressions
- Surge handling and queue bypass metrics
- Acceptance criteria for ship readiness
Action items captured separately below.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: okay, welcome everyone, gonna keep this tight. we have 75 minutes, main goal is to lock owners on the safety-net items for shipday, and make sure telemetry covers the SLOs we care about. Jordan, quick status on the bypass queue prototype?
[00:38] Jordan: yeah, um I pushed the first patch last night, it's rough, basically a reject-then-divert handler that routes heavy tails to a reserve pool. needs metrics though, no good dashboards yet.
[01:04] Claire: can you explain the reserve pool logic again? I think ops will want the memory headroom numbers up front, and the SLO math.
[01:18] Jordan: sure, so we keep a cold reserve of nodes with quantized-capable runtimes, they spin up on demand. bypass means we short-circuit batching for those requests and let them go into a smaller KV-cache-less path to avoid head-of-line blocking. it's noisy but buys latency for P99 at the cost of some cost increment.
[01:46] Ethan: small correction — the KV-cache-less path currently is missing a small piece of the attention cache restoration, so in some models you see a token duplication artifact. I found it on the 4k-quant models.
[02:06] Luis: that duplication showed up in QA too, reproduced last night, it was subtle — sometimes 1-2 tokens glitched mid-response. not catastrophic but could trigger client-side parsers.
[02:28] Maya: ok that's a potential regression. we need clear acceptance for what tolerable looks like. Claire, what thresholds do we want to set for P99 and error class?
[02:46] Claire: recommend P99 < 350ms for interactive flows, or if not possible then staged-degrade to a lower-fidelity model with a clear label. for duplication/formatting errors — any user-visible corruption above 0.2% should block. but we might make exceptions for internal launch if we state it in release notes?
[03:14] Jordan: question — is staged-degrade doable without breaking authentication and tracing? we need the request context to survive the fallback. right now we drop some of the headers when routing to reserve.
[03:33] Ethan: we can preserve headers, it's just a code path gap, I'll own a small patch. but we should test the trace continuity end-to-end.
[03:46] Maya: great, Ethan patch + test. Jordan, add a metric for header loss so we can detect in canary.
[04:02] Jordan: noted.
[04:12] Maya: telemetry — where are the biggest gaps? Claire?
[04:20] Claire: SLO burn visibility is weak. we have request counts, latency histos, but for staged-eviction and bypass routing we don't have a split by route + model-variant including quant, and we don't have the fallback reason dimension in the traces. so when something fails we can't quickly see whether it was a capacity eviction or a model fallback.
[04:50] Ethan: adding the fallback reason dimension is small in runtime, but it needs downstream changes in the tracing ingest to tag spans and the dashboard to expose a top-level filter.
[05:04] Luis: on QA side, we also need replayable traffic that triggers the exact sequence: heavy prefix -> bypass -> kernel fallback -> token duplication. I can build that test but need the right trace ids.
[05:20] Maya: action: Luis to create traffic harness; Ethan to add fallback-reason tag; Claire to wire SLO burn graphs. owners?
[05:32] Claire: I'll take SLO burn graphs.
[05:36] Ethan: I'll do fallback-reason tags and trace continuity fix.
[05:41] Luis: I'll build the harness.
[05:44] Jordan: and I'll expose bypass metrics and header-loss counter.
[05:50] Maya: perfect — put dates in action items, we need short turn.
[06:00] Jordan: one more flag — we discovered that on model X-4k-quant the kernel fallback path falls back to a very old kernel which is slower than expected; that increases latency under load. we might need a targeted kernel backport.
[06:21] Ethan: ah yes the backport — I remember. that was because the newer kernel had a regression for fused-softmax on that model. we've got a workaround but it's a perf hit.
[06:34] Claire: can we measure where the cost is worth it? i.e. cost vs latency tradeoff line for the backport vs staged-degrade.
[06:45] Maya: let's capture that in a small spreadsheet — Jordan, can you run perf delta numbers for kernel backport vs fallback path? include token/sec and P99.
[06:56] Jordan: yep, I'll do a delta run and add to the bench doc.
[07:01] Maya: FYI we also need to discuss alert noise. previously when we tuned SLO alerts they were too noisy during the canary ramp and people started auto-resolving. we don't want that.
[07:15] Claire: agreed. recommend two-tier alerts: SEV-1 for sustained SLO burn > 15 minutes plus error spike, and SEV-2 for transient blips. plus a suppression window for the initial 10 min of canary ramp.
[07:33] Ethan: but also include a root-cause hint in the alert payload — if it's a staged-eviction we should include the reserve-pool occupancy and the bypass ratio. that'll help responders triage quickly.
[07:49] Luis: can we add automated runbook links in the alert? like one click to 'invoke staged-eviction rollback' runbook?
[07:57] Maya: yes, we want that. Claire, work with runbook doc to add one-click actions.
[08:05] Claire: will do.
[08:10] Maya: timeline check: internal ship is 2026-07-30. what's realistic to be 'green' before that?
[08:19] Jordan: if we get the bypass metric and kernel perf delta by 7/28 and the harness completed by 7/30, we can run a final smoke on 7/31 — but that's tight. need earlier.
[08:31] Luis: QA needs at least two days after harness to triage flakiness. so harness by 7/27 ideally.
[08:40] Ethan: runtime fixes — small patch and tests — I can land by 7/24, but the kernel backport is higher risk and could slip to 7/29.
[08:50] Maya: ok prioritize the runtime patch and telemetry first, then the kernel. we'll treat kernel backport as a conditional mitigation. if not ready, staged-degrade must be clean.
[09:01] Jordan: we should rehearse a failure scenario — like surge + kernel fallback + loss of KV cache — and practice the rollback. schedule a table-top?
[09:11] Maya: yes, schedule a tabletop on 7/28. Claire and Jordan to lead.
[09:18] Claire: I'll prep runbook slides and the alert blamings.
[09:22] Ethan: also, a note about quantization skew — on some model variants the latency distribution changes drastically with sequence length. we need model-specific SLAs baked into the dashboard.
[09:33] Maya: add model-variant split to dashboards — Claire.
[09:37] Claire: yep.
[09:39] Maya: okay let's walk through the runbook top-level steps and call out owners.
[09:43] Maya: step 1: detect sustained SLO burn -> alert triggers and attaches runbook. owner: Claire.
[09:50] Maya: step 2: triage: inspect bypass ratio, reserve occupancy, kernel fallback rate. owner: Jordan.
[09:58] Maya: step 3: attempt automated staged-degrade to low-fidelity model or disable batching on path. owner: Ethan.
[10:07] Maya: step 4: rollback path — if automated degrade doesn't help in 10 min escalate to manual rollback and route traffic to regional failover. owner: Maya / infra ops.
[10:18] Ethan: question — region failover will require model weights sync; do we have a weight-staging plan?
[10:25] Jordan: we have partial weight syncs but not for very large models, that could take longer. fallback region should be for smaller models only. we need a gating doc.
[10:37] Luis: QA needs a section in the runbook about synthetic traffic commands to simulate failover too.
[10:43] Claire: agreed. I'll add a 'simulate' subsection — how to trigger each stage for reproducibility.
[10:50] Maya: also call out talking points for customer comms — marketing will likely want a short blurb. by default we will announce limited feature parity during initial ship.
[11:00] Jordan: on cost — the reserve pool approach adds ~8-12% infra spend under heavy tails, must be OK with finance. anyone flagged that?
[11:11] Maya: finance is aware but wants a clear cost guardrail. include a kill switch on reserve pool.
[11:18] Jordan: can implement a manual kill switch and an automatic threshold that disables reserve when cost exceeds X.
[11:24] Ethan: also think about throttling at API gateway vs runtime — throttling earlier reduces wasted cycles.
[11:30] Claire: but throttling too early impacts product experience. need a careful throttle curve.
[11:36] Maya: agreed. add throttle curve proposal to doc.
[11:40] Luis: quick QA note — a few flaky tests are timing dependent when KV cache rebuilds after staged-eviction. I'll mark them as unstable for the run.
[11:50] Maya: good call, but log them and we'll treat as known issues. make sure we annotate the release notes.
[11:58] Ethan: on the duplication artifact: I have a mitigation that inserts a post-processing sanitizer that strips simple token replays, it's a band-aid but could be used in worst case.
[12:12] Claire: if we apply sanitizer, ensure it doesn't break structured output. we need unit tests.
[12:22] Ethan: yes, will add tests.
[12:26] Maya: alright, let's summarize owners and dates.
[12:30] Maya: Jordan — bypass metric + header-loss counter + kernel perf delta by 2026-07-28.
[12:39] Jordan: got it.
[12:41] Maya: Ethan — trace continuity patch, fallback-reason tags, and duplication sanitizer tests by 2026-07-24 (sanitizer could be optional for ship).
[12:54] Ethan: ok.
[12:55] Maya: Claire — SLO burn graphs, model-variant split, inject one-click runbook links into alerts by 2026-07-24.
[13:07] Claire: will do.
[13:08] Maya: Luis — traffic harness and regression runs by 2026-07-27.
[13:14] Luis: yep.
[13:16] Maya: Maya (PM) — consolidate runbook, send to execs, schedule the tabletop for 2026-07-28.
[13:24] Maya: any other questions?
[13:27] Jordan: quick note — competitors like NimbusAI do aggressive preemption for tail mitigation; they sacrifice context a bit. just FYI as we design.
[13:38] Maya: thanks. ok let's end with immediate next steps: small patch + telemetry + harness. I'll send the meeting notes and action items after this.
[13:48] Claire: request — please include the bench doc link in the notes.
[13:52] Maya: will do. thanks everyone.
[13:55] Luis: thanks.
[13:57] Ethan: bye.

Post-meeting notes:
